terms: Section 2: a standard SAE reconstructs x̂ = W_dec f + b_dec with sparse non-negative f. Feature j has normalised decoder direction d_j and is active when f_j > 0.

Section 3: the projection p_j^(t) = d_j^T x^(t). Empirical persistence R_j(τ) is the elevation of p_j at lag τ after activation, relative to the elevation at the activating token, both measured against the mean projection. R=1 means fully retained; R=0 means back to baseline.
Section 3: the shuffled control concatenates intact sentences from different Pile documents, preserving local but not global continuity.
Section 3: context correction x̂_ctx = x̂_base + W_dec(w_τ ⊙ f^(t−τ)). R²_improve is the fraction of baseline reconstruction error this recovers on held-out data.

Section 4: Persistent SAE state h_j^(t) = λ_j h_j^(t−1) + (1−λ_j) a_j^(t), where a is the BatchTopK token-wise sparse activation. Reconstruction is x̂ = W_dec h + b_dec. h^(0) = 0 at the start of each sequence.
Section 4 / B.3: λ_j = λ_max σ(l_j), with λ_max = 0.999 and logits initialised to 0.5. The recurrence is an EMA, so the state magnitude stays bounded.
Section 5.1: slow features are the top 1% by λ_j, and fast features are the bottom 50%.
Section 5.2: relative update frequency U_{q,c} = P(token category c | active feature in quintile q) / P(c).
Section 5.4: Δ_causal is half the difference in the monitor's yes−no logit margin when adding vs subtracting a probe-weighted decoder direction v_r scaled to 10% of the hidden-state norm.
